features.notes: Auth recovery uses createRequestStateCodec and host-owned invocation facts; writes elicit auth only before invocation and entered reads require unchanged fresh classifications. Direct calls now relay downstream state inside vault encryption and the signed codec envelope, bound to principal, endpoint/pool, connector, original and resolved addresses, arguments digest, round, expiry, and a one-use storage CAS nonce. Original downstream keys stay encrypted behind numbered namespaced keys. Three prompts and a ten-minute window span auth-to-downstream composition; payload and response limits apply. Programs refuse downstream input with a direct-call nextAction. Sampling, roots, prompts, and other deferred request kinds are not relayed. Continuation failures reuse the invocation's schema-filtered snapshot and direct-call guidance requires original arguments for partial or absent echoes.

Private upward tools/list and server/discover hints and SQL-backed SDK tool/resource/template listing ResponseCacheStore honor bounded downstream TTL and intake redaction. Host auth mode constrains sharing; public hints never remove private credential, principal, pool or endpoint partitions. OAuth credential changes fence reuse within one epoch. Connection-owned notifications fence late listings, and serialized listings preserve cancellation through cleanup. Resource read payloads are never cached. Completed wire tool refreshes expose previous/new digest observations for the planned Phase 4 drift-event integration.
